content.text:
All 5 cold-start measurements taken on the Pixel 8 Pro (<REDACTED-1>, Android 16), each preceded by `nerve_kill` (force-stop, confirmed `pid: null` before the first run) and measured via Android's system-logged `ActivityTaskManager: Displayed` event — the standard cold-start metric (equivalent to `am start -W` TotalTime):

| Run | Cold start (ms) |
|---|---|
| 1 | 472 |
| 2 | 440 |
| 3 | 437 |
| 4 | 435 |
| 5 | 444 |

- **Median:** 440 ms
- **Mean:** 445.6 ms
- **Standard deviation (sample, n−1):** ≈15.1 ms (variance ≈229.3 ms²)
- **Standard deviation (population):** ≈13.5 ms (variance ≈183.4 ms²)

Runs were fairly tight except the first, which ran slightly higher (472ms) — plausibly a one-time cache/filesystem warm-up effect from the very first cold start in the session.
